This is a named P1 ask (Research.md:282; IOBoard.md:256, :280), and F14's 'otherwise' reads as a pull-down on lines that idle high. The BLHeli_S bootloader drives open-drain and high (BLHeliBootLoad.inc:70-72), so its reply's high comes from a pull-up alone. The AM32 bootloader jumps to its application when the line reads mostly low at start-up (main.c:1095-1122). Both read 2026-09-28T10:38:07Z.

The tree's 19,200 baud is a proposed analyser map (testbench/README.md:380, :396). ESCape32's wiki gives 38400 baud 8N1 (Configuration page, read 2026-09-28T10:38:07Z). IOBoard.md:263 and Research.md:282's concerns column make it a P1 ask.

IOBoard.md:282 lists the DShot rate the output path is specified for as not known. The bind list is 300 and 600 (out_bind.c:566-569), and the driver range is 150 to 1200 kbit/s (outputs.c:29). The answer halves or keeps the 0.625 µs zero-bit high.

Neither IOBoard.md nor Monostable.md states a lead length or load. The seed LSF0108 needs pull-ups on the high side ('Pull-up resistors are always required on the high side'). It states its rate at ≤30 pF and 50 pF loads (TI SDLS966M, revised May 2023, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/lsf0108.pdf, read 2026-09-28T10:44:39Z), so its rate at the connector depends on the load.

IOBoard.md:286 says the wire and line count are not stated. VESC's firmware configures separate RX and TX pins (applications/app_uartcomm.c:114-115, raw.githubusercontent.com/vedderb/bldc/master, read 2026-09-28T10:41:54Z), so one half-duplex line is not VESC's default form.

IOBoard.md:287 says the baud of iBUS, SUMD, CRSF, SRXL2 and JETI EX Bus is not stated. The owner can answer with a value or mark it for research.

IOBoard.md:287 lists whether the bench transmits on a receiver pin as not stated. Manifest.md:37-39 puts EX Bus telemetry in scope. A transmit direction changes the part from one-way to bidirectional.
IOBoard.md:279 lists whether the receiver pins pass the output gate as not known. F13's answer names the 20 output ports and the UART socket only.

The R4 row requires 'its idle level' in reset. A multiprotocol port's mode is firmware state. The pads reset pulled low with the output disabled (datasheet section 9.3, read 2026-09-28T10:39:24Z), and the expander resets with the RP2354B (IOBoard.md:340). So the row fixes no hardware level for these ports in reset. IOBoard.md:256 does give bidirectional DShot's idle as high; the gap is the reset case.

IOBoard.md:192 lists the buffer's RP2354B-side inputs and enable only (Monostable.md:88), while its first sentence covers any interlock input driven while its supply is absent. Whether a connector-side device can be powered while the board is not is not stated; a receiver's supply is open (IOBoard.md:287). The answer decides whether B-side I_off is required.
IOBoard.md:536 states that no requirement limits the current into a shorted signal line at an output connector. Research.md:282 seeds series resistance and clamps. The port rail reaches 8.7 V (F16).
IOBoard.md:65 names 'other serial devices' with no protocol, rate or level. IOBoard.md:290 and OpenYGE.md:400-403 record the ESC telemetry protocols beyond OpenYGE as an open decision.

added.question: Which protocol does a multiprotocol port carry in its ESC telemetry mode: the ESC's separate serial telemetry wire (ESC to bench only), OpenYGE (half duplex), or another? In which direction, and at what highest baud rate, in baud?
added.why: The owner's port decision lists ESC telemetry as a multiprotocol port mode (Research.md:63; IOBoard.md:64). The specification states no protocol, direction or rate for that mode. IOBoard.md:289 says whether the board reads the ESC's separate serial telemetry wire is not stated and no question asks it. IOBoard.md:290 records the telemetry protocols beyond OpenYGE as an open decision. P2 cannot check the multiprotocol path's direction, rate and bias for this mode without the answer.

added.question: When an ESC or a servo has to start up with its signal line held high to enter its bootloader or CLI, what powers it up? The choices: the operator by hand; a STOP and the operator clear of the F11 latch, since the ESC pack switch follows the enable node alone; the port's supply switch under firmware, for a servo; or a separate switch, giving its voltage in V and current in A.
added.why: The AM32 bootloader stays in the bootloader only when the line reads high at start-up and jumps to the application when it reads mostly low (AM32-bootloader bootloader/main.c:1095-1138). The BLHeli_S bootloader waits while the line is high and leaves for the application after about 250 ms from a low line (BLHeliBootLoad.inc:10, :89-99). Both read 2026-09-28T10:38:07Z. ESCape32 enters its CLI only with the line held high for 2 s on startup (wiki Configuration, read 2026-09-28T10:38:07Z). IOBoard.md:291 leaves this not stated. P2 cannot tell whether a switch is a part to qualify without the answer.
added.for_quantity: power-up of an ESC or servo for bootloader or CLI entry
